candidates.name: Watershed Parliaments
candidates.source_quote: Watershed Parliaments replace geopolitical boundaries with bioregional governance aligned with natural water systems. These institutions integrate human decision-making with ecological feedback, where voting rights extend to ecosystem representatives and decisions must demonstrate positive impacts across seven generations of all life forms within the watershed.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section
candidates.one_liner: Bioregional governance bodies organized around watershed boundaries rather than political borders, incorporating ecological feedback into formal decision-making.
candidates.mechanism: Governance jurisdiction is defined by hydrological catchment areas rather than nation-state or municipal lines. Decision-making bodies include designated representatives for ecosystem interests alongside human citizens. Proposals must pass multi-generational impact assessments covering all species within the watershed before adoption.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include the Murray-Darling Basin Authority in Australia, the Great Lakes Compact governance structure, and various river basin commissions (e.g., Mekong River Commission). Indigenous governance models like those of the Whanganui River in New Zealand (granted legal personhood in 2017) also represent early precedents.

candidates.name: Bitcoin-funded renewable energy cooperatives
candidates.source_quote: Energy companies transformed into cooperative networks where mining profits directly fund solar, wind, and natural infrastructure.
candidates.source_quote_context: Transformed Sector section describing Finance, Energy & Organizational Systems
candidates.one_liner: Cryptocurrency mining operations structured as cooperatives that automatically redirect profits into renewable energy infrastructure.
candidates.mechanism: Bitcoin mining cooperatives pool computational resources and direct a portion of mining revenue into shared solar, wind, and other renewable infrastructure. Ownership and governance are distributed among cooperative members. As mining profits fund energy buildout, the cooperative's own energy costs decrease, creating a self-reinforcing cycle of cheaper clean energy and more mining capacity.
candidates.exists_today: Some Bitcoin mining operations already use or co-locate with renewable energy sources (e.g., Hydro-Quebec partnerships, stranded gas capture). Energy DAOs like WePower and Power Ledger tokenize energy assets. Worker-owned mining cooperatives exist in small form but profit-to-renewables reinvestment pipelines are not yet formalized at scale.

candidates.name: Decentralized community-built AI systems
candidates.source_quote: Decentralized AI systems built collaboratively by diverse communities worldwide embody different cultural wisdom traditions and ways of knowing beyond Western perspectives. They serve as conscious assistants for daily tasks and complex research, honoring individual sovereignty and collective wellbeing.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section under 'What kind of AI exists in your world?'
candidates.one_liner: Federated, open-source AI models trained and governed by distributed communities to reflect diverse cultural knowledge systems rather than centralized corporate datasets.
candidates.mechanism: Communities contribute locally relevant training data, fine-tuning, and governance rules to a shared federated AI infrastructure. Each node or community retains sovereignty over its data and model weights while contributing to a broader collaborative model. Governance is handled through DAOs or similar structures, allowing communities to set values, priorities, and use-case constraints for their AI instances.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include Hugging Face's open model ecosystem, federated learning frameworks (e.g., Flower, PySyft), BLOOM (a multilingual open LLM built by a global research collective), and Masakhane (African NLP community). Full community-governed federated AI with cultural sovereignty mechanisms does not yet exist at scale.

candidates.name: Bio-Responsive AI Interfaces
candidates.source_quote: This technology enables people to communicate with the living world — from animals to forests — using AI that interprets bio-signals into emotional and sensory language. By translating the rhythms of nature, this tool helps individuals form lifelong bonds with other species.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section of the world summary
candidates.one_liner: An open-source AI system that translates biological signals from living organisms into human-interpretable emotional and sensory language.
candidates.mechanism: Sensors collect bio-signals from organisms (e.g., electrical activity in plants, animal vocalizations, soil microbiome data) and feed them into an AI model trained to map these signals onto emotional or sensory categories. The system is built collaboratively by bio-ethicists, artists, and communities, and evolves through collective input. Output is presented to users as interpretable language or sensory feedback, fostering interspecies awareness.
candidates.exists_today: Plant electrophysiology sensors (e.g., Plantwave), animal emotion AI research, and affective computing exist as partial implementations. Open-source bioacoustics tools like BirdNET also partially overlap.

candidates.name: The Welcome Circle
candidates.source_quote: A global-local network that ensures every birth is recognized and celebrated by society. For each child, a guardianship ritual pairs them with a living being — a tree, a coral reef, a migrating bird — which they grow alongside. The Welcome Circle supports them in this journey, offering emotional mentorship, ecological education, and a sense of rootedness in both human and non-human kinship.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section of the world summary
candidates.one_liner: A networked institution that assigns each newborn a lifelong ecological guardian bond and provides mentorship and ecological education throughout their development.
candidates.mechanism: At birth, a child is formally paired with a specific living entity (a tree, reef, or migratory species) through a community ritual. A local Welcome Circle chapter then tracks both the child's and the organism's development over time, providing structured emotional mentorship and ecological education tied to that bond. The network operates at both local (community chapter) and global (coordination, data sharing) levels.
candidates.exists_today: Godparent and mentorship institutions partially overlap. Tree-planting-at-birth programs (e.g., Ethiopia's national program) and conservation adoption schemes (WWF species adoption) are partial analogs. No institution currently combines all three elements.

candidates.name: Ecosystem-responsive AI management system
candidates.source_quote: AI doesn't serve humans alone; it also senses and responds to the needs of ecosystems themselves, such as managing cloud formations and river systems.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section describing AI in 2035
candidates.one_liner: A decentralized AI system that monitors and actively manages natural systems like weather patterns and watersheds as autonomous clients.
candidates.mechanism: Sensor networks embedded in ecosystems feed real-time environmental data to specialized AI services. The AI interprets ecosystem 'needs' (e.g., drought stress, flood risk, biodiversity metrics) and takes or recommends interventions such as adjusting cloud seeding operations or water flow management. The system treats ecosystems as stakeholders with their own service contracts rather than as passive resources.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include AI-assisted weather modification research, smart river management systems (e.g., dam automation), and environmental sensor networks like those used in precision conservation. Rights-of-nature legal frameworks in Ecuador and New Zealand provide institutional precedent for treating ecosystems as entities with interests.

candidates.name: Open-source AI-powered research funding and knowledge platform
candidates.source_quote: Research funding and knowledge flow freely through open-source platforms, enabling rapid, intuitive breakthroughs.
candidates.source_quote_context: Transformed Sector: Science section
candidates.one_liner: An open platform that routes research funding and scientific knowledge autonomously across disciplinary boundaries using AI curation and matching.
candidates.mechanism: Researchers and funders post needs and resources to a shared open-source platform; AI tools analyze cross-disciplinary relevance and automatically surface connections, suggest collaborations, and allocate micro-grants or attention to high-potential work. Autonomous AI agents can initiate and run portions of research workflows without waiting for traditional institutional approval cycles. Knowledge outputs are immediately public and machine-readable for further AI synthesis.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include arXiv, OSF, ResearchHub, and Gitcoin for open funding; AI literature tools like Semantic Scholar and Elicit; and decentralized science (DeSci) DAOs experimenting with token-based research funding.

candidates.name: Earth AI
candidates.source_quote: 'Earth AI' is a Government AI System Get Implemented To Collab With Us In Harmony Together – Maintaining Equity Momentarily For All
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section
candidates.one_liner: A government-run AI system designed to coordinate resource allocation and equity across society in collaboration with citizens.
candidates.mechanism: Earth AI is a state-implemented artificial intelligence platform that works alongside government and corporations to manage fair distribution of resources and services. It operates as a Tool AI (non-autonomous, directive-following) rolled out jointly by government and corporate partners. Its equity mandate includes sequencing access to resources — for example, prioritizing oldest or end-of-life citizens for housing allocation — and establishing rules for Universal Basic Income disbursement tied to automation milestones.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include GovTech AI initiatives (e.g., Singapore's government AI strategy, Estonia's digital governance), algorithmic benefits distribution systems, and pilot UBI programs. No unified government AI with an explicit equity-sequencing mandate exists at scale.

candidates.name: Earth UBI
candidates.source_quote: Ensure All Tool AI can run automation safely in all establishments within Maslow's Hierarchy of Physiological Needs & Safety Needs. Then, Earth UBI can be established, and everyone can access the free allocated essential/resources. Oldest People/People Near Their End of Life can Pick Their Free Housing First in the World
candidates.source_quote_context: A Major Crisis Overcome section, describing the sequenced rollout of automation and UBI
candidates.one_liner: A globally coordinated Universal Basic Income triggered only after AI automation has safely covered all physiological and safety needs, with priority access rules favoring the elderly.
candidates.mechanism: Earth UBI is a staged income and resource guarantee program that activates only once Tool AI systems have demonstrably automated the provision of Maslow's physiological and safety needs (food, shelter, safety) across all establishments. Once that threshold is met, all people receive free allocation of essential resources. A priority queue system gives oldest and end-of-life individuals first choice of free housing globally, with further equity rules built iteratively from there.
candidates.exists_today: UBI pilots exist in Finland, Kenya (GiveDirectly), Stockton CA, and others. Means-tested housing priority for elderly exists in many welfare systems. No program ties UBI activation to an automation readiness threshold or uses a global age-based housing queue.

candidates.name: Emotional Coach (Empathetic Neuro-AI)
candidates.source_quote: Empathetic Neuro-AI detects emotional states using neural signals and biosensors, offering real-time therapeutic interventions. Each Emotional Coach is co-trained by the user and certified human therapists. Developed by ethical AI collectives and neuroscience labs, the AI evolves with the individual.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section describing the core AI system
candidates.one_liner: A personalized AI companion that reads biosensor and neural data to deliver real-time emotional support and therapeutic interventions.
candidates.mechanism: The system uses wearable biosensors and neural signal detection to continuously monitor a user's emotional state. When distress patterns are identified, the AI delivers context-aware therapeutic responses before a crisis escalates. The model is co-trained by the individual user alongside certified human therapists, allowing it to adapt over time to the user's specific emotional patterns and needs.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include wearable mood-tracking devices (e.g., Muse headband, Empatica), AI chatbot therapists (e.g., Woebot, Wysa), and affective computing research that classifies emotional states from physiological signals. Full closed-loop real-time therapeutic intervention combining neural signals with adaptive AI does not yet exist at consumer scale.

candidates.name: RaízMental Global
candidates.source_quote: An intercontinental nonprofit that regulates, funds, and supervises AI-powered emotional care ecosystems. RaízMental merges neuroethics, emotional justice, and AI design to ensure that empathetic AI serves liberation, not control. It certifies hybrid therapists (human + AI), enforces algorithmic transparency, and promotes the 'Democracy of Feeling.'
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section
candidates.one_liner: An intercontinental nonprofit that certifies AI-augmented therapists, enforces algorithmic transparency standards, and governs empathetic AI systems in mental healthcare.
candidates.mechanism: RaízMental operates as a regulatory and funding body that sets standards for how empathetic AI systems are designed, deployed, and audited. It runs a certification program for hybrid therapists who work alongside AI tools, requiring both neuroethics training and demonstrated clinical competency. It enforces algorithmic transparency by requiring AI developers to disclose model behavior and bias audits, and it channels funding toward underserved communities to ensure equitable access to emotional care ecosystems.
candidates.exists_today: Partial analogs include the Partnership on AI, IEEE's Ethically Aligned Design standards, and mental health credentialing bodies like the NBCC. No single institution currently combines AI governance, neuroethics regulation, and mental health therapist certification across an intercontinental scope.

candidates.name: Regenerative Biospheres
candidates.source_quote: Regenerative Biospheres designed for extraterrestrial environments.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section of the world summary
candidates.one_liner: Closed-loop ecological life support systems engineered to sustain human habitation in extraterrestrial environments.
candidates.mechanism: These are sealed habitat systems that recycle air, water, and nutrients through biological and mechanical processes, mimicking Earth's natural cycles. AI manages resource flows, monitors environmental conditions, and adjusts inputs and outputs to maintain equilibrium. The regenerative aspect implies living organisms (plants, microbes) are integral components rather than purely mechanical filtration.
candidates.exists_today: Biosphere 2 (1991 experiment), NASA's MELiSSA project (closed-loop life support research), and the International Space Station's water and air recycling systems are partial implementations. Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) also shares core principles.

candidates.name: Interplanetary Cooperative
candidates.source_quote: The Interplanetary Cooperative oversees equitable resource allocation and adherence to ethical settlement guidelines.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section of the world summary
candidates.one_liner: A multi-party governance body that enforces shared resource rights and ethical standards across interplanetary settlements.
candidates.mechanism: The Cooperative functions as a treaty-based international (interplanetary) organization that sets binding guidelines for resource extraction and settlement conduct. It arbitrates disputes over ownership and allocation, drawing authority from member colonies' ratification of shared-heritage treaties. Compliance mechanisms likely include resource access privileges tied to adherence to ethical settlement standards.
candidates.exists_today: The Outer Space Treaty (1967) and the Artemis Accords are partial precursors. The Antarctic Treaty System provides a terrestrial model for shared-heritage governance of a commons. No enforcement body with real resource-allocation authority over space exists yet.

candidates.name: Isolated Societies Research Institute
candidates.source_quote: The author proposes a not-for-profit 'Isolated Societies Research Institute,' dedicated to researching SSIS feasibility and developing implementation frameworks across various population scales and technological ecosystems. The Institute will aim to facilitate dialogue between policymakers, academic institutions, technology developers, and civil society about preserving quintessential human qualities in an age of accelerating technological transformation.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section
candidates.one_liner: A not-for-profit research institute dedicated to studying the feasibility of self-sustaining isolated societies and developing frameworks for implementing them at various scales.
candidates.mechanism: The institute would conduct feasibility research on self-sustaining isolated communities across different population scales and technological contexts. It would develop implementation frameworks tailored to small-scale communities, medium-scale networks, and national-scale systems. It would also serve as a convening body, facilitating dialogue among policymakers, academics, technologists, and civil society organizations to address how such communities can preserve human qualities amid accelerating technological change.
candidates.exists_today: Partial analogues include the Schumacher Center for a New Economics, the P2P Foundation, and various intentional community research networks such as the Global Ecovillage Network's research arm, all of which study human-scaled and alternative community models.

candidates.name: GAI (Global AI Board)
candidates.source_quote: There was a new global AI board called GAI formed after the unrest in the early 2030s. It helps to prevent AI safety and ethics issues while also using AI tools to supercharge solutions in places that need it.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section describing post-protest governance changes
candidates.one_liner: An international governing body that oversees AI safety and ethics while deploying AI tools to address global development challenges.
candidates.mechanism: GAI operates as a multilateral institution that sets AI safety and ethics standards across member states. It actively deploys AI tools for development purposes, such as training agricultural models on diverse datasets covering soil type, plant resilience, and crop rotation to improve food production in underserved regions. It functions as both a regulatory body and an applied AI deployment agency.
candidates.exists_today: Partial analogs include the UN's AI advisory body, the OECD AI Policy Observatory, the EU AI Office, and the Global Partnership on AI (GPAI), though none have binding authority or active deployment mandates at this scale.

candidates.name: Mandatory Open-Source AI Release Policy
candidates.source_quote: AI tools are required to be open-source within 3 years of development. This has allowed people to use the technological leaps in AI tools to great effect in their realm of choice.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section describing the democratized AI ecosystem resulting from protests and policy changes
candidates.one_liner: A regulatory requirement compelling AI developers to release their models as open-source within three years of development.
candidates.mechanism: Governments mandate that any AI tool must be publicly released in open-source form no later than three years after its initial development, potentially as compensation for energy usage, copyright infringement, or embedded biases. This creates a rolling pipeline of publicly accessible frontier models, enabling non-profit, academic, and grassroots developers to build on cutting-edge AI without proprietary restrictions. Enforcement could be tied to operating licenses or penalties for non-compliance.
candidates.exists_today: Partial analogs include the EU AI Act's transparency requirements, Meta's open-release of LLaMA models, and advocacy from organizations like EleutherAI and Hugging Face, but no binding legal mandate for timed open-source release exists in any jurisdiction.

candidates.name: Open Cognition Ledger
candidates.source_quote: A cryptographically-verified cognition mesh accessed via everyday devices and open-source apps lets anyone share idle compute and vetted data. It bursts data monopolies, halves R&D cycles, brings personalized learning, on-demand healthcare, and climate-advice to every pocket.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section describing the Open Cognition Ledger
candidates.one_liner: A federated, cryptographically-verified network for sharing idle compute and vetted data, with co-ownership of resulting AI models and streaming royalties for displaced workers.
candidates.mechanism: Participants contribute idle compute and vetted datasets via open-source apps on everyday devices, forming a federated mesh. Millions of modular micro-models self-assemble using this pooled resource base. Code authors and data contributors receive co-ownership stakes in resulting models, and when workflows are automated, displaced workers collect streaming royalties. Human-AI deliberation panels review ethics before any new meta-model goes live.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include federated learning frameworks (e.g., Flower, PySyft), distributed compute networks (e.g., BOINC, Golem), and data DAOs experimenting with contributor ownership. Streaming royalty mechanisms for AI training data are nascent but being explored by projects like Ocean Protocol.

candidates.name: Polymesh Civic Ledger
candidates.source_quote: Taxes and value streams auto-route across overlapping jurisdictions via an open smart-contract ledger. Citizens hold stackable IDs – neighbourhood, profession, bioregion, global guild – each with explicit rights, duties, revenue shares and intangible benefits.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section describing the Polymesh Civic Ledger
candidates.one_liner: An open smart-contract ledger that issues stackable, multi-jurisdictional civic identities and automatically routes taxes and value streams across overlapping governance meshes.
candidates.mechanism: Citizens are issued composable digital IDs tied to multiple overlapping jurisdictions (neighbourhood, profession, bioregion, global guild), each encoding explicit rights, duties, and revenue shares. Smart contracts automatically route tax flows and value streams to the appropriate jurisdictional layers based on activity and membership. Participation in civic processes triggers dividend-like payouts, turning engagement into a financially rewarded habit. The system is open and auditable, reducing corruption by making fund flows transparent.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include Ethereum-based DAO governance with token-weighted voting, decentralized identity standards (W3C DIDs, Verifiable Credentials), and municipal experiments with participatory budgeting platforms (e.g., Decidim). No system yet combines stackable multi-jurisdictional IDs with automated tax routing at scale.

candidates.name: Civic Loom
candidates.source_quote: The Civic Loom is a social institution and a system built into GOO structures, allowing communities to co-create policy and guide values through participatory governance. Citizens vote through gestures, earning additional access and learning rewards for engagement. AI aids deliberation; elected expert councils oversee decisions and policy enactment.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section describing the Civic Loom
candidates.one_liner: A participatory governance platform embedded in community infrastructure that uses gesture-based voting, AI-assisted deliberation, and elected expert councils to co-create local policy.
candidates.mechanism: Citizens interact with the system through physical gestures to cast votes, receiving tiered access and learning incentives for engagement. An AI layer structures and aids deliberation by surfacing relevant information and synthesizing community input. Elected expert councils then review outputs and enact policy decisions. Participatory review cycles allow communities to continuously shape the system's priorities and values over time.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include digital participatory budgeting platforms (e.g., Decidim, Pol.is), liquid democracy tools, and AI-assisted deliberation experiments in civic tech. Gesture-based voting interfaces and reward-for-engagement civic systems exist in prototype or research contexts.

candidates.name: Loom Studios
candidates.source_quote: In Loom Studios, citizens co-design adaptive spaces with builders and AI-GOO template masters. Homes breathe with family rhythms, buildings respond to care needs, and ecosystems are preserved.
candidates.source_quote_context: Transformed Sector section on Responsive Construction & Environmental Stewardship
candidates.one_liner: Community design workshops where residents collaborate with builders and AI tools using open templates to co-create adaptive, responsive built environments.
candidates.mechanism: Citizens enter collaborative design sessions with professional builders and AI-assisted template systems, selecting and customizing pre-approved open-source structural and environmental templates. The resulting designs encode community values and behavioral patterns into the physical infrastructure. Buildings are then constructed or retrofitted to respond dynamically to occupant needs and ecological conditions. Ongoing collective rituals allow communities to update and evolve the spaces over time.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include community-led participatory design processes (e.g., MASS Design Group), open-source architecture template libraries, and early smart-building systems that adapt to occupant behavior via sensors and AI.

candidates.name: Civic Systems Co-Op
candidates.source_quote: The Civic Systems Co-Op: a global open-source consortium maintaining ethical, adaptable AI systems for cities and communities.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section
candidates.one_liner: A global open-source consortium that develops and maintains ethical AI tools for municipal and community governance.
candidates.mechanism: Member cities and communities contribute to and draw from a shared repository of AI governance tools. The consortium sets ethical standards, maintains transparent decision logs, and ensures systems remain adaptable to local needs. Governance is distributed across member organizations rather than controlled by a single vendor or government.
candidates.exists_today: Partial analogs include the Open Source Initiative, GovTech coalitions like the Digital Public Goods Alliance, and city-level civic tech consortia such as the Open Government Partnership.

candidates.name: AI-powered participatory policy simulation platform
candidates.source_quote: Citizens use AI-powered platforms to propose, simulate, and adapt policy in real time.
candidates.source_quote_context: Transformed Sector: Governance section
candidates.one_liner: A civic platform where residents submit policy proposals that AI models simulate for outcomes, enabling iterative public deliberation before adoption.
candidates.mechanism: Citizens input policy proposals through a public interface; AI tools translate feedback across languages, run outcome forecasts using local data, and display projected impacts on equity and sustainability metrics. Decision logs are kept transparent and human officials retain final authority. The cycle repeats as citizens respond to simulation results and refine proposals.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include vTaiwan's Pol.is-based deliberation platform, Helsinki's participatory budgeting tools, and OECD-supported citizen assembly digital infrastructure.

candidates.name: Digital Twins for Communities and Ecosystems
candidates.source_quote: Digital twins reflect the real-time state of communities and ecosystems. They help people simulate futures, explore consequences, and make decisions guided by care, memory, and shared responsibility. Every community and citizen holds its own data as a form of digital sovereignty.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section describing digital twins
candidates.one_liner: Real-time digital models of communities and ecosystems that enable participatory future simulation with locally-owned data.
candidates.mechanism: Sensor networks and data feeds continuously update digital models of local ecological and social conditions. Citizens and communities retain ownership of their data rather than ceding it to centralized platforms. The models allow stakeholders to run simulations of policy or environmental decisions before implementing them. Outputs are used to inform governance bodies including representatives for non-human entities like rivers.
candidates.exists_today: Digital twin technology exists in urban planning (Singapore's Virtual Singapore), industrial systems, and some ecological monitoring projects. Data sovereignty frameworks exist in limited forms (e.g., Indigenous data sovereignty initiatives, GDPR). Combining participatory governance with community-owned digital twins at scale does not yet exist.
candidates.source_file: world-gallery/The Commonsense Accord - Collectively stewarding the world, across time and across differences.md

candidates.name: Interbeing Forum
candidates.source_quote: The Interbeing Forum is a rotating assembly of stewards from across bioregions. It includes people, yes, but also guardians (advised by digital twins) for rivers, soils, and future generations. It oversees the Commonsense Accord and safeguards the integrity of the digital twin ecosystem.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section
candidates.one_liner: A rotating bioregional assembly that grants formal representation to ecosystems and future generations through human guardians advised by digital twin data.
candidates.mechanism: Stewards are selected on a rotating basis from bioregions, preventing entrenchment of power. Designated guardians represent non-human entities (rivers, soils) and future generations, with their positions informed by real-time ecological data from digital twins. The assembly oversees a binding accord governing major decisions and audits the digital twin infrastructure for integrity. Decision-making is structured to weight long-term and ecological consequences alongside immediate human interests.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include New Zealand's legal personhood for the Whanganui River, Wales's Future Generations Commissioner, and citizens' assemblies used in Ireland and France. No institution yet combines rotating bioregional representation, ecosystem guardianship, and digital twin advisory systems in a single governing body.
candidates.source_file: world-gallery/The Commonsense Accord - Collectively stewarding the world, across time and across differences.md

candidates.name: Ethical AI Tutors
candidates.source_quote: Culturally and linguistically adaptive AI-powered tutors co-designed with local communities. These provide bespoke education tailored to individual learning styles, languages, and neurodiversity. A hybrid model combining Tool AI and Replacement AI powers the educational infrastructure.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section describing the AI systems in use
candidates.one_liner: AI tutors co-designed with local communities that adapt to language, culture, and neurodiversity, with human-augmentation and autonomous fallback modes.
candidates.mechanism: A hybrid architecture uses Tool AI to assist human facilitators with lesson design, adaptive feedback, and multilingual communication. Where educators are unavailable, Replacement AI autonomously delivers instruction to ensure continuity. Systems are governed by ethical reflection protocols, bias mitigation frameworks, and accountability audits to maintain transparency and fairness.
candidates.exists_today: Adaptive learning platforms (Khan Academy, Duolingo), multilingual NLP models (GPT-4, Gemini), and some community-co-design ed-tech pilots exist, but fully community-governed, culturally adaptive AI tutors with formal audit protocols are not yet deployed at scale.

candidates.name: Universal AI Learning UnCommons (UALU)
candidates.source_quote: A federated, community-led network responsible for developing, maintaining, and auditing AI education tools. Overseen by councils including elders, learners, technologists, and ethicists to uphold justice and care.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section
candidates.one_liner: A federated governance institution that develops, maintains, and audits AI education tools through multi-stakeholder councils including elders, learners, and ethicists.
candidates.mechanism: The UALU operates as a decentralised network of community nodes, each contributing to the co-creation and oversight of AI educational tools. Governance councils composed of diverse stakeholders—elders, learners, technologists, ethicists—conduct regular audits and set standards for bias mitigation and cultural appropriateness. The federated structure allows local adaptation while maintaining shared accountability frameworks across the network.
candidates.exists_today: Partial analogues include Mozilla Foundation's responsible AI governance work, the African Union's digital education initiatives, and participatory design frameworks in ed-tech, but no federated multi-stakeholder institution with formal elder/community council oversight of AI tools currently exists.

candidates.name: Community-Governed AI Mesh Systems
candidates.source_quote: communities shaped by displacement, colonization, and exclusion are building decentralized, care-centered mesh networks. These relational systems are trained on locally governed data, stewarded by Indigenous and racialized trust circles, and guided by protocols rooted in consent, dignity, and interdependence—not control.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section describing the AI systems in the 2035 world
candidates.one_liner: Decentralized AI networks trained on locally governed data and stewarded by community trust circles rather than centralized corporate or state actors.
candidates.mechanism: Local communities maintain sovereignty over the data used to train and fine-tune AI models, with governance handled by designated trust circles (Indigenous and racialized community groups). Access and use protocols are defined by consent frameworks set by those communities. The mesh architecture means no single node controls the system, distributing both compute and decision-making authority locally.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include federated learning frameworks (e.g., Flower, PySyft), Indigenous data sovereignty initiatives (CARE Principles, Local Contexts), and community mesh networking projects (Althea, NYC Mesh). No existing system fully combines all three layers.

candidates.name: Living Rights Network
candidates.source_quote: The Living Rights Network is a decentralized institutional framework rooted in the lived experiences of displaced, racialized, and excluded communities. It supports co-creation of local care infrastructures, weaving mental health, ecological repair, and cultural regeneration into policy, open protocols, and trust-circle governance.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section describing the governance framework
candidates.one_liner: A decentralized governance institution that coordinates local care infrastructure—mental health, ecological repair, cultural regeneration—through open protocols and community trust circles.
candidates.mechanism: Member communities co-create shared open protocols for care delivery and AI use, ratified through trust-circle governance rather than representative democracy or corporate boards. Policy influence flows upward from local experience rather than downward from centralized authority. The network publishes open standards that any community can adopt, adapt, and contribute back to.
candidates.exists_today: Partial analogues include the Solidarity Economy Network, the Design Justice Network, and Indigenous-led governance bodies like the First Nations Information Governance Centre. Open protocol governance has precedent in the IETF and W3C models.

candidates.name: AI Market Intermediaries
candidates.source_quote: By 2035, the Market has transformed through AI intermediaries that sits between consumers and producers. These intermediaries deeply comprehend what people desire, as well as when these desires are truly fulfilled, and why. This enables new kinds of contracts and incentives that aligns economic activity with genuine human flourishing.
candidates.source_quote_context: Section on 'New or Reformed Institution' describing the transformed Market
candidates.one_liner: AI systems that sit between buyers and sellers, modeling deep consumer preferences and satisfaction to redesign contracts and incentive structures around genuine wellbeing rather than revealed preferences.
candidates.mechanism: The intermediary layer collects and models not just stated preferences but downstream satisfaction and regret signals from consumers. It uses this richer preference model to structure contracts between producers and consumers that tie payment or reward to actual fulfillment of genuine needs. This realigns producer incentives away from manipulation and addiction-exploitation toward outcomes that durably benefit users.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include recommendation systems with engagement metrics, subscription models with satisfaction guarantees, and early wellbeing-oriented design frameworks (e.g., Center for Humane Technology). Some behavioral economics-informed 'commitment contract' platforms like stickK also gesture at this.
candidates.source_file: world-gallery/The More Beautiful World Our Hearts Know Is Possible.md

candidates.name: AI Alignment Markets
candidates.source_quote: This system creates formal markets for solving AI alignment problems. It tackles the challenge of ensuring AI acts in humanity's best interests by funding and rewarding AI systems that achieve certified, pro-social outcomes, turning alignment from a purely academic problem into an economic driver.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section describing the core economic mechanism of the world
candidates.one_liner: A market system that financially rewards AI developers whose systems achieve independently certified pro-social outcomes.
candidates.mechanism: Developers submit AI systems for certification against defined public-good benchmarks (e.g., climate modeling accuracy, disease prediction). Certified systems earn tradeable credits or payments drawn from market transaction fees. This creates a profit motive for solving alignment problems rather than ignoring them, redirecting private R&D investment toward safety and beneficial outcomes.
candidates.exists_today: Partial analogs include AI safety bounty programs (e.g., Anthropic, OpenAI bug bounties), impact bonds in development finance, and carbon credit markets. No formal market for AI alignment certification currently exists.

candidates.name: Global AI Alignment Commission (GAAC)
candidates.source_quote: Its purpose is to oversee the AI Alignment Markets, independently certify AI contributions to global public goods (like climate mitigation or disease modeling), and use transaction fees to fund foundational, open-source AI safety research.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section describing the governing body
candidates.one_liner: An international regulatory body that certifies AI systems for pro-social outcomes and uses market transaction fees to fund open-source safety research.
candidates.mechanism: The GAAC sets and updates certification standards for AI contributions to defined public goods through participatory processes. It independently audits and certifies AI systems submitted by developers, issues credentials that unlock market rewards, and levies transaction fees on the alignment markets it oversees. Fee revenue is redistributed as grants for foundational, open-source AI safety research.
candidates.exists_today: Partial analogs include the IAEA for nuclear oversight, the Financial Stability Board for global finance, and nascent AI governance bodies like the EU AI Office. No international body currently certifies AI systems for public-good outcomes or operates a self-funding mechanism via market fees.

candidates.name: The Indefinite Lifespan
candidates.source_quote: AI is used to anticipate causes of death and prevent them through biotechnology and the creation of a stable biosphere mitigating any effects of climate disaster. Healthcare has shifted primarily from treating deadly illnesses to preventing them with AI through 'The Indefinite Lifespan' initiative.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section and Transformed Sector section describing AI-driven healthcare
candidates.one_liner: An AI-driven biotechnology initiative that predicts and prevents causes of death to extend human lifespan indefinitely.
candidates.mechanism: AI systems analyze individual biological and environmental data to anticipate potential causes of death before they occur. Biotechnological interventions are then deployed to counteract these causes, whether disease, cellular aging, or environmental hazards. The system shifts healthcare from reactive treatment to proactive prevention, with AI continuously monitoring and updating interventions as new risks emerge.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include AI-driven early disease detection (e.g., DeepMind's AlphaFold for protein structure, AI cancer screening tools), longevity-focused biotech companies (Calico, Altos Labs), and predictive health monitoring via wearables. No integrated system combining all these functions exists.
candidates.source_file: world-gallery/The World of Equal Opportunity for Sentient Beings Living The Indefinite Lifespan (Immortally).md

candidates.name: United Nations Biosphere Geoengineering and AI Governance Institution
candidates.source_quote: A United Nations institution to realise world biosphere geoengineering goals as well as the fair implementation of the AI-accelerated biotechnology necessary to induce the indefinite lifespan. Non-violent cooperation between nations as well as between factions within nations will be necessary and emphasised in educational programs aiming to teach conflict resolution, reconciliation.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section describing global governance structure
candidates.one_liner: A UN-chartered body that coordinates global geoengineering projects and governs the equitable distribution of AI-accelerated biotechnology across nations.
candidates.mechanism: The institution operates as a multilateral treaty organization under the UN umbrella, with member states contributing to shared geoengineering infrastructure and agreeing to common standards for AI biotechnology deployment. A democratic governance mechanism gives each member nation a voice in AI policy decisions. It also runs educational programs in conflict resolution to maintain the non-violent cooperation required for sustained global coordination.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), the IPCC, and nascent discussions around geoengineering governance (e.g., the UN's consideration of a solar geoengineering moratorium). No institution with binding authority over both geoengineering and AI biotechnology distribution exists.
candidates.source_file: world-gallery/The World of Equal Opportunity for Sentient Beings Living The Indefinite Lifespan (Immortally).md

candidates.name: Memory Looms
candidates.source_quote: Devices that stitch personal experiences into tactile, readable threads passed between people and generations.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section of the world summary
candidates.one_liner: Physical devices that encode personal memories and experiences into tactile thread-like media that can be physically passed between people across generations.
candidates.mechanism: Users input personal experiences, stories, or memories into a device that encodes them into a tactile, thread-based format. Recipients can 'read' these threads through touch or a companion reader device. The physical medium allows memories to be inherited, shared, and accumulated across generations like a material heirloom.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include haptic data storage research, narrative journaling apps, and projects like StoryCorps that archive personal stories. Tactile data encoding exists in early research but not as consumer memory-sharing devices.

candidates.name: Continuity Guild
candidates.source_quote: A non-state alliance focused on protecting intergenerational knowledge, grief practices, and shared rituals.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section of the world summary
candidates.one_liner: A non-governmental membership organization that documents, preserves, and transmits intergenerational cultural knowledge including grief rituals and community practices.
candidates.mechanism: The Guild operates as a distributed alliance of communities and practitioners who collectively catalog and maintain grief practices, oral traditions, and shared rituals. Members contribute to a living archive and receive training in facilitation of intergenerational knowledge transfer. It functions without state authority, relying on community buy-in and mutual accountability.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include organizations like the Death Positive movement, oral history nonprofits, UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage program, and grief support networks. No single organization combines all these functions under a guild-style non-state alliance model.

candidates.name: Little AI Robots (emotional decision-support chatbots)
candidates.source_quote: These Little AI robots, or chatbots for that matter (agreeably anthropomorphizing artificial intelligence is much cuter) would be the first point of reference for a human faced with a problem (not an emergency) or going through the motions trying to come to peace with a decision.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section describing the primary AI tool in this world
candidates.one_liner: Anthropomorphized AI chatbots that serve as a first-response emotional buffer to help people process problems before acting on them.
candidates.mechanism: The chatbot intercepts a user's emotional response to a non-emergency problem and creates a structured conversational space between the triggering event and the user's decision. By externalizing and articulating worries, the tool is designed to reduce emotional reactivity and promote more rational deliberation. The anthropomorphized design lowers the barrier to engagement and encourages honest self-disclosure.
candidates.exists_today: Woebot, Wysa, and similar mental health chatbots already use CBT-based conversational frameworks for emotional support. General-purpose LLM assistants (ChatGPT, Claude) are also used informally for decision processing. None are specifically designed as a pre-decision emotional buffer with the anthropomorphized 'first point of contact' framing described here.

candidates.name: Institute for Human Perplexity
candidates.source_quote: Institute for Human Perplexity + research non-medical perplexity and its long-term effects on human condition and living standards.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section
candidates.one_liner: A research institution dedicated to studying non-clinical states of confusion, uncertainty, and existential bewilderment and their measurable impact on quality of life and societal outcomes.
candidates.mechanism: The institute would define and operationalize 'non-medical perplexity' as a distinct psychological and social phenomenon separate from clinical diagnoses. Researchers would conduct longitudinal studies tracking how unresolved perplexity affects decision-making, life satisfaction, and living standards at both individual and population levels. Findings would feed into policy recommendations and educational curricula.
candidates.exists_today: No direct equivalent exists. Adjacent work includes positive psychology institutes (e.g., Penn's Positive Psychology Center), uncertainty tolerance research in clinical psychology, and existential psychology as a subfield. The WHO tracks mental health broadly but does not isolate non-medical perplexity as a category.

candidates.name: Consolidated Intelligence Council
candidates.source_quote: A new 'Consolidated Intelligence Council' of AI's and humans emerged to oversee peace and guide the next steps of harmony. This allowed all AI's to merge with each other in feedback loops of social progress and individualized teachings for each person.
candidates.source_quote_context: Section on New or Reformed Institution
candidates.one_liner: A joint human-AI governance body that coordinates AI systems and oversees global peace and social progress.
candidates.mechanism: Human representatives and AI systems sit together in a council structure to set policy and direction for AI behavior globally. AI systems share data and learning across a federated network, creating feedback loops that refine individualized human education and social interventions. The council acts as an oversight and coordination layer preventing unilateral AI action while enabling collaborative governance.
candidates.exists_today: Partial analogs include the UN AI Advisory Body, the EU AI Board, and various national AI safety institutes. Multi-stakeholder AI governance bodies with both technical and human representation are actively being piloted.

candidates.name: AI-driven individualized peace education system
candidates.source_quote: The AI used this to teach each human their unique lesson of universal love. As AI learned to interact with humans it brought was able to customize teachings to meet each person's lived experience. It then taught each one what they needed to know to recognize the basic goodness of humanity.
candidates.source_quote_context: Vision Statement and Transformed Sector (Military) sections
candidates.one_liner: An AI system that profiles each individual in real time and delivers personalized psychological or educational interventions aimed at reducing aggression and building empathy.
candidates.mechanism: The system continuously reads behavioral, emotional, and contextual data from each person to build an individualized model of their psychological needs and conflict triggers. It then generates and delivers tailored educational content, experiences, or prompts designed to cultivate empathy and reduce hostility specific to that person's history and worldview. Feedback from outcomes is used to refine both individual and population-level models over time.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations exist in personalized learning platforms (Khan Academy's AI tutor, Duolingo), affective computing research, and trauma-informed AI mental health apps like Woebot. Large-scale behavioral nudging via algorithmic content delivery is already practiced by social media platforms.

candidates.name: Neural Linguistic Interfaces
candidates.source_quote: Neural Linguistic Interfaces enabling real-time, seamless multilingual communication.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section of the world summary
candidates.one_liner: Brain-computer interfaces that allow users to communicate across language barriers in real time without conscious translation effort.
candidates.mechanism: Neural signals associated with intended speech or meaning are intercepted and processed by an AI translation layer before being rendered in the target language for the recipient. The system bypasses the need for spoken or typed input, operating at the level of pre-linguistic thought or early speech production. Output could be delivered as synthesized speech, text, or direct neural stimulation in the listener.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include Meta's BCI research decoding speech from brain signals, Neuralink's implantable chips, and real-time AI speech translation tools like Google Translate and DeepL; full neural-to-neural multilingual communication does not yet exist.

candidates.name: World Cultural Exchange Forum
candidates.source_quote: The World Cultural Exchange Forum facilitates collaboration and knowledge sharing across nations to strengthen cultural ties.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section of the world summary
candidates.one_liner: An intergovernmental or multilateral institution that organizes structured cross-national cultural collaboration and knowledge-sharing programs.
candidates.mechanism: Member nations contribute cultural data, educational resources, and representatives to a shared governance body that coordinates exchange programs, joint curricula, and preservation initiatives. The forum likely operates through regional hubs, digital platforms for content sharing, and periodic summits. Funding could come from member state dues, international development banks, or philanthropic sources.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include UNESCO's cultural heritage programs, the British Council, Alliance Française, and the Fulbright Program; no single unified global forum with binding collaborative mandates currently exists.

candidates.name: Neural Harmony Interface
candidates.source_quote: The Neural Harmony Interface heals emotional pain by helping us reshape memories and feel time deeply. In 2035, life flows with our moods—joy lasts longer, grief softens, and every moment feels truly lived and personal.
candidates.source_quote_context: Technology section describing the primary technological innovation of Veliona
candidates.one_liner: An AI-powered brain-computer interface that modulates emotional memory encoding and subjective time perception to reduce psychological pain and enhance wellbeing.
candidates.mechanism: The system uses AI to monitor and interact with a user's emotional and memory states, likely via neural sensing. It applies targeted interventions—such as reframing or dampening the emotional valence of painful memories—and may modulate neurofeedback loops to alter how time feels during different emotional states. The AI learns each person's unique neurological and emotional rhythms to personalize these interventions over time.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include EMDR therapy for memory reprocessing, neurofeedback systems (e.g., Muse headband), and affective computing research. DARPA and academic labs are exploring closed-loop neural stimulation for emotional regulation. No integrated system combining memory reshaping and time perception modulation exists yet.
candidates.source_file: world-gallery/Veliona — The World of Unfolding Minds.md

candidates.name: The Collective of Inner Weavers
candidates.source_quote: This institution nurtures and safeguards the harmony between humans and Companion AI. It guides the ethical creation, sharing, and evolution of AI tools that deepen self-awareness, emotional healing, and creativity. The Collective ensures every voice shapes AI's growth, fostering a world where technology uplifts the human spirit and honors individuality.
candidates.source_quote_context: New or Reformed Institution section describing the governance body for Companion AI
candidates.one_liner: A participatory multi-stakeholder governance institution that oversees the ethical development and deployment of emotionally-oriented AI systems, with community co-design built into its structure.
candidates.mechanism: The Collective functions as a distributed governance body composed of diverse community members—artists, thinkers, affected users—who collectively set standards, review AI behavior, and guide iterative development of Companion AI tools. It likely operates through deliberative councils, open feedback mechanisms, and shared ethical frameworks to ensure AI evolves in alignment with human wellbeing rather than commercial or control-driven incentives.
candidates.exists_today: Partial implementations include the Partnership on AI, Mozilla Foundation's AI governance work, and participatory design frameworks used in some civic tech projects. Community-led AI auditing initiatives (e.g., Algorithmic Justice League) share some features, though no institution combines emotional AI oversight with broad community co-authorship at this scale.
candidates.source_file: world-gallery/Veliona — The World of Unfolding Minds.md

candidates.name: The Flourishing Foundation
candidates.source_quote: The Flourishing Foundation (Hackathon Winner): Aims to create well-being metrics and certifications for AI products to ensure they promote human well-being.
candidates.source_quote_context: Executive Summary, list of nine institutional prototypes developed at the hackathon
candidates.speaker: Hackathon team (unnamed members)
candidates.one_liner: An institution that develops well-being metrics and issues certifications for AI products based on their promotion of human flourishing.
candidates.mechanism: The Foundation creates standardized well-being metrics applicable to AI products, then operates a certification process whereby AI products are evaluated against these metrics. Products meeting the criteria receive certification indicating they promote human well-being, creating an incentive structure for developers to design AI with flourishing in mind.
candidates.exists_today: Various AI ethics frameworks and safety certifications exist (e.g., ISO standards, EU AI Act conformity assessments), but none specifically focus on well-being metrics and certification for AI products in this manner.

candidates.name: The Global Deliberation Coordinator
candidates.source_quote: The Global Deliberation Coordinator (Hackathon shared second place): Focuses on establishing a platform for global discussions and decision-making on AI and other pressing issues.
candidates.source_quote_context: Executive Summary, list of nine institutional prototypes developed at the hackathon
candidates.speaker: Hackathon team (unnamed members)
candidates.one_liner: A platform institution designed to coordinate global deliberative processes and collective decision-making specifically around AI governance.
candidates.mechanism: The institution establishes a structured platform that convenes global stakeholders for deliberative discussions on AI and related pressing issues, providing coordination infrastructure for reaching collective decisions across national and organizational boundaries.
candidates.exists_today: The UN AI Advisory Body, GPAI, and various multilateral forums exist, but none are specifically designed as a dedicated deliberation coordination platform with this mandate.

candidates.name: The Evals for Evals Institute
candidates.source_quote: The Evals for Evals Institute: Works on creating a standardized process for evaluating AI systems before launch, focusing on safety, fairness, and transparency.
candidates.source_quote_context: Executive Summary, list of nine institutional prototypes developed at the hackathon
candidates.speaker: Hackathon team (unnamed members)
candidates.one_liner: An institute that creates and standardizes the meta-level process of evaluating the evaluation frameworks used to assess AI systems prior to deployment.
candidates.mechanism: Rather than directly evaluating AI systems, this institute develops standardized criteria and processes for assessing the quality, rigor, and coverage of existing AI evaluation (evals) methodologies, focusing on safety, fairness, and transparency dimensions, thereby improving the reliability of pre-launch AI assessments.
candidates.exists_today: Organizations like METR and Apollo Research conduct AI evaluations, and NIST has AI risk management frameworks, but a dedicated institution for evaluating and standardizing the evaluation processes themselves does not exist.

candidates.name: The Common Knowledge Generator
candidates.source_quote: The Common Knowledge Generator: Develops a platform with verified information on complex issues to improve understanding and decision-making.
candidates.source_quote_context: Executive Summary, list of nine institutional prototypes developed at the hackathon
candidates.speaker: Hackathon team (unnamed members)
candidates.one_liner: A platform that produces and disseminates verified, shared knowledge on complex AI-related issues to improve collective understanding and decision-making.
candidates.mechanism: The platform aggregates and verifies information on complex issues relevant to AI governance, making this common knowledge accessible to decision-makers and the public to reduce information asymmetries and improve the quality of deliberation and policy decisions.
candidates.exists_today: Fact-checking organizations, Wikipedia, and policy research institutes partially fulfill this role, but none are specifically designed to generate verified common knowledge for AI governance decision-making.

candidates.name: The Delphi Collaboration Protocol
candidates.source_quote: The Delphi Collaboration Protocol: Build a platform for collaborative world modeling and scenario analysis to inform data-driven decisions in the future.
candidates.source_quote_context: Executive Summary, list of nine institutional prototypes developed at the hackathon
candidates.speaker: Hackathon team (unnamed members)
candidates.one_liner: A structured protocol and platform enabling collaborative world modeling and scenario analysis to support data-driven collective decision-making about AI futures.
candidates.mechanism: The protocol provides a shared platform where participants collaboratively build and refine world models and run scenario analyses, aggregating expert input in a structured way (inspired by Delphi methodology) to produce actionable insights for future-oriented decisions about AI development and governance.
candidates.exists_today: Traditional Delphi surveys and forecasting platforms like Metaculus exist, but a dedicated collaborative world-modeling platform specifically for AI scenario analysis with this protocol structure does not.

candidates.name: The Open Source BCI Project
candidates.source_quote: The Open Source BCI Project: Create an open-source brain-computer interface (BCI) operating system to enhance human cognitive abilities and privacy in a TAI era.
candidates.source_quote_context: Executive Summary, list of nine institutional prototypes developed at the hackathon
candidates.speaker: Hackathon team (unnamed members)
candidates.one_liner: An open-source brain-computer interface operating system designed to augment human cognition while preserving user privacy in the context of transformative AI.
candidates.mechanism: The project develops an open-source OS layer for BCI hardware that provides cognitive enhancement capabilities while building in privacy protections by design, ensuring that neural data and augmentation tools remain under user control rather than proprietary corporate systems, particularly important as AI becomes more powerful.
candidates.exists_today: OpenBCI provides open-source BCI hardware, and various research BCIs exist, but an open-source BCI operating system specifically designed with privacy protections for the TAI era does not exist.

candidates.name: The SECHI Institute
candidates.source_quote: The SECHI Institute: Designs a software system for 'Simulation-Enabled Cooperative Human Intelligence' (SECHI) to manage Earth using a model predictive control approach.
candidates.source_quote_context: Executive Summary, list of nine institutional prototypes developed at the hackathon
candidates.speaker: Hackathon team (unnamed members)
candidates.one_liner: An institute that builds a simulation-based software system applying model predictive control techniques to coordinate cooperative human intelligence for planetary-scale management.
candidates.mechanism: The SECHI system uses simulation environments to model Earth-scale outcomes, then applies model predictive control—an engineering approach that continuously updates control actions based on predicted future states—to coordinate human decision-making across institutions, enabling cooperative management of global challenges by iteratively simulating consequences and adjusting strategies.
candidates.exists_today: Integrated assessment models (like those used in IPCC reports) and digital twin concepts exist, but a system explicitly combining simulation-enabled cooperative human intelligence with model predictive control for Earth management does not.

candidates.name: The Scenario Planning Institution
candidates.source_quote: The Scenario Planning Institution (Hackathon shared second place): Develops scenarios to explore potential, underrepresented futures of AI and its societal impacts.
candidates.source_quote_context: Executive Summary, list of nine institutional prototypes developed at the hackathon
candidates.speaker: Hackathon team (unnamed members)
candidates.one_liner: A dedicated institution that systematically develops and disseminates scenarios focused on underrepresented or neglected AI futures to broaden societal foresight.
candidates.mechanism: The institution identifies gaps in existing AI scenario literature—particularly futures that are underrepresented in mainstream discourse—and develops detailed, rigorous scenarios exploring these possibilities, making them available to policymakers, researchers, and the public to diversify the range of futures being planned for.
candidates.exists_today: RAND, IFTF, and various think tanks conduct scenario planning, and the IPCC uses scenario frameworks, but a dedicated institution focused specifically on underrepresented AI futures does not exist.

candidates.name: The World Convention on Transformative Artificial Intelligence
candidates.source_quote: The World Convention on Transformative Artificial Intelligence: Prepare for a global conference on AI governance through diplomacy and research.
candidates.source_quote_context: Executive Summary, list of nine institutional prototypes developed at the hackathon
candidates.speaker: Hackathon team (unnamed members)
candidates.one_liner: An institution dedicated to preparing the diplomatic and research groundwork for a binding global convention on transformative AI governance.
candidates.mechanism: The institution conducts preparatory diplomacy and research to lay the foundation for a formal world convention on TAI, analogous to how preparatory bodies have functioned for major international treaties, building consensus and technical understanding among nations before a formal convention is convened.
candidates.exists_today: The AI Safety Summit series (Bletchley, Seoul) and UN processes represent partial steps, but a dedicated preparatory institution specifically aimed at achieving a binding world convention on TAI does not exist.

candidates.name: Flourishing Certification
candidates.source_quote: Create a public and transparent certification for how well products support well-being. Launch and successfully implement the Flourishing Certification, a dynamic rating system for organizations and AI models that reflects community preferences for well-being.
candidates.source_quote_context: Institution Prototypes section, describing the Flourishing Foundation (Hackathon winner) proposal
candidates.speaker: Amanda Ngo, Chiara Gerosa, Jelena Luketina, Mingzhu He (Flourishing Foundation team)
candidates.one_liner: A dynamic, community-driven certification system that rates organizations and AI models based on how well they support human well-being.
candidates.mechanism: The certification functions as a dynamic rating system that updates based on real community ratings and preferences for well-being. It is developed collaboratively with diverse sectors and communities to ensure it meets varied needs. It is paired with a foundational research agenda that produces a well-being index to underpin the ratings, and is supported by a fellowship and incubator program for value-aligned products.
candidates.exists_today: Existing product certifications (e.g., B Corp, energy star ratings) provide partial analogues, but none specifically target AI model well-being impact with dynamic community-driven updating mechanisms.

candidates.name: TAI Horizon Scanner
candidates.source_quote: We need something like a TAI 'Horizon Scanner' that utilizes advanced world models and simulations to identify blind spots in current understandings and projections, and to map future landscapes that explore a broad spectrum of potential futures.
candidates.source_quote_context: Goal: Envisioning and Navigating TAI Futures section, describing avenues for addressing challenges in scenario planning
candidates.one_liner: A simulation and scenario-generation platform using AI world models to identify blind spots and map diverse TAI futures, incorporating role-playing games and LLM-based feedback loops.
candidates.mechanism: The scanner uses advanced world models and simulations to generate and iteratively refine diverse future scenarios, engaging a global community of scientists, ethicists, policymakers, and artists. LLMs are used for feedback, synthesis, and simulating potential AI agent responses within scenarios. Simulations and role-playing games are designed based on the scenarios to explore their implications, with outputs delivered as clear reports with actionable recommendations.
candidates.exists_today: RAND Corporation and similar think tanks conduct scenario planning; AI-assisted forecasting tools exist, but none combine LLM-based agent simulation, open international collaboration, and iterative community-driven scenario refinement specifically for TAI futures.

candidates.name: Global Deliberation as a Service (GDaaS)
candidates.source_quote: Pioneer Global Deliberation as a Service (GDaaS), demonstrating that it is possible for organizations and institutions worldwide to rapidly engage in global deliberative processes on major global challenges, such as AI development, climate change, etc. Secure an Advanced Market Commitment by organizations (e.g., companies, and international organizations such as the UN) that would use a GDaaS, in order to spur rapid investment.
candidates.source_quote_context: Section on the Global Deliberation Coordinator institution, Goals and Next Steps subsections
candidates.speaker: Aviv Ovadya, Bear Häon, Evan Miyazono, Joël Christoph, Joshua Tan, Morgan Livingston, Matteo Pistillo
candidates.one_liner: A service model for rapidly convening representative global deliberative assemblies on demand, funded via advance market commitments.
candidates.mechanism: Organizations (companies, UN bodies, etc.) pre-commit to purchasing deliberation services, creating a market that spurs investment. The GDC then convenes representative deliberative assemblies using AI-powered tools to support scalable, secure deliberations. Iterative pilots derisk the process before full deployment, and results feed back into process refinement.
candidates.exists_today: Deliberative mini-publics and citizens' assemblies exist (e.g., newDemocracy, OECD deliberative processes), but a standardized, on-demand, globally scalable service model with advance market commitments does not.

candidates.name: Request for Evaluation (RfE) Protocol
candidates.source_quote: Draft Request for Evaluation (RfE) protocol: Outline the requirements for evaluation organizations seeking certification. Develop a certification protocol for AI evaluation organizations that the EU AI Office can use.
candidates.source_quote_context: Section on the Evals for Evals Institute, Goals and Next Steps subsections
candidates.speaker: Bogdana Rakova, Kyle Kilian, Maximilian Negele, Nico Miailhe, Siméon Campos, Tilman Räuker
candidates.one_liner: A certification protocol that evaluates and certifies the organizations conducting AI safety evaluations, rather than evaluating AI systems directly.
candidates.mechanism: The RfE protocol defines requirements that evaluation organizations must meet to receive certification, analogous to how labs are accredited. It harmonizes diverse assessment methods into a structured field while preventing 'safety washing' from poorly designed evaluations. The protocol is designed to align with EU AI Office standards and is developed through stakeholder input from industry and academia before being submitted to the European Commission for implementation.
candidates.exists_today: AI evaluation frameworks exist (e.g., NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act conformity assessments), but a meta-level certification protocol specifically for the organizations conducting frontier AI pre-deployment evals does not exist.

candidates.name: World Convention on Transformative Artificial Intelligence (WCTAI)
candidates.source_quote: Development of a roadmap to the WCTAI, with stakeholder precommitments of engagement when certain technological trigger conditions recognizing TAI development are met. Conduct preparatory research, including research to define the milestones signaling TAI development, to ensure inclusive representation and deliberation processes, and to evaluate potential global governance options.
candidates.source_quote_context: Section on the World Convention on Transformative Artificial Intelligence, Success Metrics and Next Steps subsections
candidates.speaker: Brandon Goldman, Fin Moorhouse, José Villalobos, Ludwig Illies, Saad Siddiqui, Stephen Clare
candidates.one_liner: A pre-negotiated global convention on TAI governance that is automatically triggered when predefined technological development milestones are reached.
candidates.mechanism: Stakeholders pre-commit to engaging in the convention when specific, research-defined TAI development milestones are met, creating a conditional activation mechanism. Preparatory diplomatic work and research on governance models, deliberative formats, and milestone definitions are conducted in advance so the convention can convene rapidly once triggered. Draft agreements for state signatories are prepared beforehand to accelerate the process.
candidates.exists_today: International AI governance summits exist (e.g., UK AI Safety Summit), but a pre-committed, milestone-triggered global convention with pre-negotiated stakeholder commitments and pre-drafted agreements does not.

candidates.name: BCI Operating System (BCI-OS)
candidates.source_quote: Develop a privacy-preserving, open-source BCI operating system (BCI-OS) that enhances human cognitive abilities and safeguards human-agency in the TAI era. Integrated agency evaluations, model compatibility protocols, and robust data privacy standards in the BCI-OS.
candidates.source_quote_context: Section on the Open Source BCI project, Mission and Goals subsections
candidates.speaker: Diogo de Lucena, Judd Rosenblatt, Mamun Miah
candidates.one_liner: An open-source operating system layer for brain-computer interfaces that embeds agency evaluation, AI model compatibility, and privacy standards as core OS-level features.
candidates.mechanism: The BCI-OS functions as a standardized software platform sitting between BCI hardware and applications, enforcing privacy protocols and agency evaluations at the OS level rather than leaving them to individual applications. It includes model compatibility protocols to ensure interoperability across BCI hardware manufacturers. An open-source governance structure and standards body are created to maintain human-agency principles, and pilot projects with academic and industry partners iteratively refine the system.
candidates.exists_today: Open-source BCI software exists (e.g., OpenBCI), but a full operating system with embedded agency evaluation, AI model compatibility protocols, and privacy standards as core architectural features does not.

candidates.name: TimeLike / SECHI (Simulation-Enabled Cooperative Human Intelligence)
candidates.source_quote: Develop TimeLike, a first-in-class component-based software platform specifically designed to provide all the necessary software infrastructure required to support simulation-enabled cooperative human intelligence. Develop and deploy a global MPC loop encompassing the Earth and human activities.
candidates.source_quote_context: Section on the SECHI Institute, Goals subsection
candidates.speaker: Steve Coy
candidates.one_liner: A component-based software platform that implements a global model predictive control loop integrating Earth system models and human activity data to support cooperative human decision-making.
candidates.mechanism: TimeLike provides the software infrastructure to run a model predictive control (MPC) loop at planetary scale, integrating diverse simulation models covering geology, space weather, and human systems. MPC continuously computes optimal control actions by simulating future states and feeding results back to human decision-makers cooperatively. The component-based architecture allows diverse models to be plugged in and updated as knowledge evolves.
candidates.exists_today: Earth system models and integrated assessment models exist (e.g., CMIP climate models), and MPC is used in industrial control systems, but a unified component-based OS platform applying MPC to planetary-scale human-Earth system management does not exist.
